scope: 409 retained staged further problems only; exclude every existing cut problem. Complete or matching announced resolutions are archived without allocating an AIM ID. Surviving open targets receive consecutive IDs from 666 only after their status gate passes.

records.title: Sharp minimax rates for a Darcy conductivity
records.review_note: The First Proof batch-3 human theorem treats a sufficiently small Holder-Zygmund ball about the constant conductivity and identifies a rate only up to logarithmic factors. It does not treat this fixed general Sobolev ball with unrestricted allowed amplitude and sharp unsquared expected loss including logarithms. The source Theorem 13 still explicitly leaves the general Sobolev reconstruction rate open.
records.current_title: Sharp minimax rates for a Darcy conductivity
records.area: Bayesian inverse problems and uncertainty quantification

records.title: Does Cameron–Martin coercivity ensure a strong posterior mode?
records.review_note: The uniform positive Cameron-Martin quadratic margin is retained. The current v4 small-ball classification has the previously checked counterexamples, whose Onsager-Machlup functions fail this coercivity. Weak modes and strong modes under the stronger ambient lower bound do not settle the proposed general strong-mode conclusion. Fresh author, primary-record and indexed announcement searches found no matching complete result.
records.current_title: Does Cameron–Martin coercivity ensure a strong posterior mode?
records.area: Bayesian inverse problems and infinite-dimensional probability

records.title: Harmonic-prior predictive dominance with unknown variance
records.review_note: The fixed harmonic prior and replicated unknown-variance experiment are essential. Known-covariance harmonic prediction and ordinary-KL unknown-variance results have different hypotheses or endpoint loss. Fresh searches including indexed proof venues found no full interior-alpha unknown-variance dominance theorem or counterexample.
records.current_title: Harmonic-prior predictive dominance with unknown variance
records.area: Bayesian statistical prediction and uncertainty quantification

records.title: Does metric completion preserve minimal Sobolev gradients?
records.review_note: The completion question asks for equality of the minimal gradients, not equivalence of Sobolev definitions on a complete space. Path-almost-open special cases remain stronger assumptions. The 2026 S-gradient/Hajlasz characterization and single-test-plan results do not imply exact preservation for every noncomplete doubling PI space. No matching full resolution located.
records.current_title: Does metric completion preserve minimal Sobolev gradients?
records.area: Nonlinear potential theory on metric spaces

records.title: Sharp local integrability of complex m-subharmonic functions
records.review_note: Lin v2 retains the sharp strict exponent as a conjecture and supplies capacity or finite-energy conditions, not every local m-subharmonic function. Quaternionic, compact-Hermitian weaker-exponent and false-endpoint statements are distinct. No matching complete result or announcement found. Clarify the standard exclusion of the identically minus-infinite function when preparing the canonical page.
records.current_title: Sharp local integrability of complex m-subharmonic functions

records.title: Are all isometries of the Mabuchi completion induced by smooth Kähler-potential isometries?
records.review_note: The original completion-isometry question was reopened in the primary text. Darvas classifies differentiable smooth-space isometries, not arbitrary surjective completion isometries. The current author list includes 2026 entropy and geodesic-line papers without a matching classification announcement. Indexed public-venue and later-result searches found no complete resolution.
records.current_title: Are all isometries of the Mabuchi completion induced by smooth Kähler-potential isometries?

records.title: Algebraicity of the three-dimensional two-source quadrature domain
records.review_note: The target is the canonical three-dimensional equal-positive-point-source obstacle domain for every a>1. Four-dimensional Neumann ovaloids and nonalgebraic evaluation-plus-derivative domains, planar algebraic Schwarz reflections and approximate three-dimensional sink descriptions do not answer it. No matching exact three-dimensional algebraicity or nonalgebraicity proof found in the fresh searches.
records.current_title: Algebraicity of the three-dimensional two-source quadrature domain
records.area: Potential theory and free boundary problems

records.title: Cluster values on the complex $\ell_p$ ball
records.review_note: The same-ball cluster equality at nonzero interior points of complex ell-p for p different from 2 remains distinct from origin, sphere, Hilbert and enlarged-radius bounded-type results. The prior all-space positive proof was invalidated by its published corrigendum. Fresh author/subject searches surfaced fibre geometry and corrected older statements, not a matching new complete theorem.
records.current_title: Cluster values on the complex $`\ell_p`$ ball

records.title: One shared value with multiplicity among four meromorphic shared values
records.review_note: The current v8 primary retains the two-infinite-order case as Conjecture 1. Its finite-order theorem, the two-CM theorem, and five-shared-pair results do not settle one-CM/three-IM at arbitrary growth. Fresh later-result and public-venue searches found no matching complete announcement.
records.current_title: One shared value with multiplicity among four meromorphic shared values

records.title: Gradient propagation of smallness below codimension one
records.review_note: The reopened Foster-Gallegos primary gives the power estimate for harmonic functions and only a stretched-logarithmic modulus with general Lipschitz coefficients. Its explicit nonanalytic-coefficient limitation matches the remaining target; later elliptic interface or planar results do not cover every n>=3 and every positive delta. No full matching result located.
records.current_title: Gradient propagation of smallness below codimension one
records.area: Elliptic PDE and quantitative unique continuation

records.title: Attenuating the singularities of positive closed currents by finite modifications
records.review_note: The primary survey asks for one finite modification controlling every residual Lelong number. Xia b-divisor/cohomological approximation permits varying models or representatives and is not this exact fixed-current attenuation. The OpenAI zero-Lelong results concern special nef adjoints and boundary hypotheses, not arbitrary positive closed currents. No matching complete general theorem found.
records.current_title: Attenuating the singularities of positive closed currents by finite modifications

records.title: The sharp Landau image-disk constant
records.review_note: Recent October univalent Bloch-Landau improvements, including the current arXiv and Zenodo certificates, impose injectivity and do not give the sharp image-disk constant for every holomorphic function. Bounded/harmonic Landau-radius and prescribed-center problems are different. No exact lower bound matching the Rademacher upper candidate was found.
records.current_title: The sharp Landau image-disk constant

records.title: Sharp exponential volume decay for plurisubharmonic sublevel sets
records.review_note: Question 35 removes the polynomial prefactor while retaining the critical exponential rate and diameter/mass dependence. Real Monge-Ampere torsion, complex energy-integrability and complex-Sobolev capacity results do not imply that critical weak-tail estimate. No matching complete resolution or announcement located in the fresh named-question and broader venue searches.
records.current_title: Sharp exponential volume decay for plurisubharmonic sublevel sets

records.title: The square-root factorial multiplier sequence
records.review_note: The current primary record remains the 2015 v2 source. Sector-reducing and other classical Bessel multiplier results do not prove that sqrt(k)/k! preserves real zeros in every degree. A right-half-plane zero exclusion is weaker than Laguerre-Polya membership. Fresh problem-number, author, coefficient and venue searches found no matching all-degree solution.
records.current_title: The square-root factorial multiplier sequence
records.area: Polynomial zero preservation and entire functions

records.title: Maximal arclength of polynomial lemniscates in every degree
records.review_note: Tao proves the maximizer only in sufficiently high degree. The author blog, current problem discussion and computational repository still leave degrees outside the established cases; an initial small-degree certification claim does not cover every remaining degree. Minimal area and shortest-path lemniscate papers answer different questions. No complete all-degree announcement located.
records.current_title: Maximal arclength of polynomial lemniscates in every degree

records.title: Positive capacity of transcendental quasiregular backward-orbit closures
records.review_note: The closed backward-orbit capacity question remains for arbitrary entire transcendental quasiregular maps in dimensions >=3. At-least-one-pole theorems, polynomial-type and commuting-map theorems have different assumptions; no-pits-effect and local-index cases do not cover the target. Fresh author, subject and proof-venue searches found no complete result.
records.current_title: Positive capacity of transcendental quasiregular backward-orbit closures
records.area: Geometric function theory and nonlinear potential theory

records.title: Real-rootedness of real powers of binomial coefficients
records.review_note: The September published conjecture covers all degrees and all real powers at least two. The Evidence Press quartic candidate only addresses degree four, and asymptotic free-probability results do not supply the missing uniform finite-degree assertion.
records.current_title: Real-rootedness of real powers of binomial coefficients

records.title: Algebraicity criterion for nonsingular rational differential equations
records.review_note: Lam and Litt retain bounded integrality on the current Problems I Like page. Special Picard-Fuchs and isomonodromy cases do not settle arbitrary nonsingular rational ODEs with finitely many denominator primes.
records.current_title: Algebraicity criterion for nonsingular rational differential equations

records.title: Ampleness of strictly nef anti-log canonical divisors
records.review_note: The current OpenAI numerical-semiampleness theorem explicitly requires K_X+B to be pseudo-effective. For this strictly nef anti-log-canonical target K_X+Delta is the negative of a nonzero strictly nef divisor, so that hypothesis is unavailable. Generalized minimal models, threefold ampleness and rational connectedness do not prove all-dimensional ampleness. No matching full resolution or announcement located.
records.current_title: Ampleness of strictly nef anti-log canonical divisors

records.title: Sharp-degree hyperbolicity of generic projective hypersurfaces
records.review_note: The 30 October source review is reused and the current author manuscript was located again: its predicted sharp Zariski-open degree threshold is still a conjecture. Sufficiently-high-degree theorems and the degree-17 surface result do not reach degree 5 or the all-dimensional threshold 2n-1. Canonical ampleness assuming hyperbolicity is the reverse direction. No matching new full announcement found.
records.current_title: Sharp-degree hyperbolicity of generic projective hypersurfaces

records.title: Boundary-pole decay of the pluricomplex Green function
records.review_note: The target is compact-uniform decay as the pole approaches an arbitrary hyperconvex boundary. Lipschitz-boundary results, Lp decay and continuity in the other Green-function argument do not give this.
records.current_title: Boundary-pole decay of the pluricomplex Green function

records.title: Does polynomial Fischer surjectivity force a quadratic-order degree bound?
records.review_note: The newer planar result addresses n=2 and k=1. The target ranges over every dimension and every polyharmonic order; complex-coefficient counterexamples and bounded-degree surjectivity assumptions differ.
records.current_title: Does polynomial Fischer surjectivity force a quadratic-order degree bound?
records.area: Complex analysis and potential theory; polyharmonic equations

records.title: Interior regularity of a single-pole pluricomplex Green function
records.review_note: The target requires an interior failure of C2 regularity away from a single pole on a smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain. Two-pole bidisc examples, failures at the boundary and examples requiring only C2 rather than smooth boundary do not match. The indexed Pome page could not be fetched; its description alone is not treated as a counterexample.
records.current_title: Interior regularity of a single-pole pluricomplex Green function

records.title: A sharp affine-modulus bound for harmonic homeomorphisms
records.review_note: The September Kalaj-Liu-Zhu examples disprove an upper distortion bound and satisfy the present lower bound. Higher-dimensional annular results and the known circular planar case do not settle arbitrary doubly connected planar domains.
records.current_title: A sharp affine-modulus bound for harmonic homeomorphisms
records.area: Complex analysis and geometric function theory

records.title: A Smirnov function without a Hilbert-domain holomorphic extension
records.review_note: The target is extension from the infinite-dimensional Smirnov class to the Hilbert polydisc. Hardy-class extension and unrelated one-variable or vector-measure results do not answer the published Question 2.28. No matching later complete announcement was located.
records.current_title: A Smirnov function without a Hilbert-domain holomorphic extension
records.area: Infinite-variable complex analysis and function spaces

records.title: Finite-time singularities of the Chern–Ricci flow
records.review_note: The Hermitian null-locus results impose lower-volume and metric or bounded-mass hypotheses. Kähler surface Type I theorems and Chern holonomy flows do not settle arbitrary Hermitian finite-time singularities.
records.current_title: Finite-time singularities of the Chern–Ricci flow
records.area: Complex analysis, geometric analysis and nonlinear PDEs

records.title: Half-Hölder extension of the Brjuno-corrected infimum radius
records.review_note: The target concerns the infimum over all injective germs. High-type quadratic Siegel-radius results and bounded comparison with that radius do not imply the required uniform half-Holder extension for the infimum.
records.current_title: Half-Hölder extension of the Brjuno-corrected infimum radius

records.title: An analytic twist map with an irrational invariant circle that is not C1
records.review_note: The newly inspected October 26 paper 2610.35068, Theorem C(ii), constructs analytic rough irrational invariant graphs for dissipative maps with lambda strictly between zero and one. These maps are not area preserving, so they do not answer the present conservative global twist-map question. The October 15 invariant-graph paper and failure of C2-plus-epsilon regularity also do not supply failure of C1.
records.current_title: An analytic twist map with an irrational invariant circle that is not C1

records.title: Does a strict Laguerre inequality for every imaginary translate force real zeros?
records.review_note: The strict ordinary Laguerre inequality for every nonzero shift is essential. Known results with finitely many nonreal zeros, extra real-zero density, or all higher Laguerre inequalities impose additional conditions. No matching general resolution of Conjecture 3.5 was located.
records.current_title: Does a strict Laguerre inequality for every imaginary translate force real zeros?

records.title: Fatou flowers for isolated tangent-to-identity germs in higher dimension
records.review_note: The October survey still retains dimensions at least three with only degenerate characteristic directions. Dimension two, a nondegenerate direction, or a stronger formal separatrix hypothesis does not give the unrestricted flower assertion.
records.current_title: Fatou flowers for isolated tangent-to-identity germs in higher dimension

records.title: Sharp-degree hyperbolicity of generic hypersurface complements
records.review_note: The current sharp logarithmic conjecture uses a nonempty Zariski-open set and degree at least 2n+1 for a single smooth hypersurface complement. High-degree and very-general results, two-component boundaries and compact hypersurface hyperbolicity do not supply this exact statement.
records.current_title: Sharp-degree hyperbolicity of generic hypersurface complements

records.title: Which zero, pole and one-point divisors can a meromorphic disk function realise?
records.review_note: The original Bergweiler-Eremenko interpolation problem asks for a criterion for every finite triple of zero, pole and one-point divisors. Special two-point configurations, Goldberg constant estimates and radial-value problems do not give such a characterization.
records.current_title: Which zero, pole and one-point divisors can a meromorphic disk function realise?

records.title: Brown–Shields cyclicity in the classical Dirichlet space
records.review_note: The current weighted Dirichlet-space papers have additional space, measure or zero-set hypotheses. They do not settle Brown-Shields cyclicity for arbitrary outer functions in the classical Dirichlet space with radial zero set of logarithmic capacity zero.
records.current_title: Brown–Shields cyclicity in the classical Dirichlet space
records.area: Complex analysis, potential theory and operator theory

records.title: Does positive Favard length force positive analytic capacity?
records.review_note: The September random-Cantor paper and ICM survey retain the arbitrary compact-set implication. Counterexamples with zero Favard length and positive analytic capacity concern the converse. Sigma-finite length and extra projection-density hypotheses are absent here.
records.current_title: Does positive Favard length force positive analytic capacity?
records.area: Complex analysis and geometric measure theory

records.title: Does every open Riemann surface embed properly in the complex plane of dimension two?
records.review_note: The current author statement still distinguishes general proper C3 embeddings and C2 immersions from proper C2 embeddings. Results for already embedded bordered surfaces or particular topology do not cover every fixed open Riemann surface.
records.current_title: Does every open Riemann surface embed properly in the complex plane of dimension two?

records.title: Smooth Levi-flat hypersurfaces in the complex projective plane
records.review_note: The specialist survey reports gaps in historical general CP2 claims. Homogeneous or real-analytic examples, singular Levi-flats and dimension at least three do not settle compact smooth boundaryless Levi-flat hypersurfaces in CP2.
records.current_title: Smooth Levi-flat hypersurfaces in the complex projective plane

records.title: Vekua's harmonic boundary problem in connectivity at least three
records.review_note: Arbitrary componentwise boundary fluxes on a bounded domain are required. Steklov proportionality, a common signed normal derivative, and unbounded hollow-vortex constructions impose different conditions.
records.current_title: Vekua's harmonic boundary problem in connectivity at least three
records.area: Potential theory and free boundary problems

records.title: Talenti comparison for complex Monge–Ampère equations in a ball
records.review_note: The original Talenti paper disproves a general-domain analogue but retains its ball conjecture. Real Monge-Ampere rearrangements and extra rotational invariance do not settle arbitrary continuous ball densities.
records.current_title: Talenti comparison for complex Monge–Ampère equations in a ball

records.title: Can every Blaschke product be uniformly approximated by interpolating Blaschke products?
records.review_note: Algebra generation by interpolating Blaschke products and approximation by quotients or products do not imply approximation by a single interpolating Blaschke product in the full disk supremum norm.
records.current_title: Can every Blaschke product be uniformly approximated by interpolating Blaschke products?

records.title: Boundary Hölder regularity of harmonic quasiconformal maps on arbitrary domains
records.review_note: The fresh 2602.05436 theorem requires C1-alpha Lyapunov source and target domains; the present target has arbitrary bounded source domain and preserves its boundary exponent. Uniform-perfectness results remain restricted.
records.current_title: Boundary Hölder regularity of harmonic quasiconformal maps on arbitrary domains
records.area: Complex analysis and geometric function theory

records.title: Relative proper embedding of a punctured closed disc in the affine plane
records.review_note: Proper embeddings of punctured open discs do not give the relative closed-disc-minus-point approximation and compact-set avoidance required here. Bordered-surface theorems have a different source domain.
records.current_title: Relative proper embedding of a punctured closed disc in the affine plane

records.title: Smooth Chern–Ricci collapse on non-Kähler elliptic bundles
records.review_note: The May general-type surface theorem has Kodaira dimension two and Gromov-Hausdorff conclusions; this elliptic-bundle question requires global smooth tensor convergence and normalized full-curvature bounds for arbitrary Gauduchon data.
records.current_title: Smooth Chern–Ricci collapse on non-Kähler elliptic bundles
records.area: Complex geometry and geometric partial differential equations

records.title: The critical opening for asymptotic Borel surjectivity
records.review_note: The critical opening, Roumieu quantifiers and three different asymptotic classes are retained. Interior/exterior bounds, rational-index exclusions and Beurling statements do not settle both unrestricted endpoint decisions.
records.current_title: The critical opening for asymptotic Borel surjectivity

records.title: Moderate measures and Hölder continuous Monge–Ampère potentials
records.review_note: A moderate measure is weaker than having a Holder super-potential. The available Hermitian continuous-solution theorem and sufficient Holder characterizations do not establish Holder potentials for every moderate measure.
records.current_title: Moderate measures and Hölder continuous Monge–Ampère potentials

records.title: Are polynomial Fischer operators bijective on all entire functions?
records.review_note: Current Fischer decompositions impose growth restrictions, use only the principal homogeneous part or give existence without uniqueness. The target uses the whole conjugated polynomial and every entire forcing, with uniqueness.
records.current_title: Are polynomial Fischer operators bijective on all entire functions?
records.area: Complex analysis and potential theory; holomorphic partial differential equations

records.title: Unions of conformally removable compact sets
records.review_note: The exact gap concerns overlapping arbitrary conformally removable compacta. Special SLE curves, disjoint unions and rigidity of circle domains with already removable boundaries do not prove general union closure.
records.current_title: Unions of conformally removable compact sets
records.area: Complex analysis, conformal geometry and potential theory

records.title: Characterize the Bloch-norm closure of bounded analytic functions
records.review_note: Finite Hardy-exponent and BMO closure characterizations do not cover H-infinity. The Limani-Nicolau weight counterexample refutes a proposed characterization rather than supplying the missing general one.
records.current_title: Characterize the Bloch-norm closure of bounded analytic functions

records.title: Higher-dimensional asymptotic attraction rates of holomorphic germs
records.review_note: The current attraction-rate results found concern dimension two or restricted higher-dimensional normal forms. They do not give a degree-at-most-n algebraic integer and uniform exponential comparability for every dominant singular germ.
records.current_title: Higher-dimensional asymptotic attraction rates of holomorphic germs

records.title: Universal harmonic-measure spectra and simple connectivity
records.review_note: The target compares dimension-sublevel spectra over arbitrary versus simply connected planar domains. Brennan inverse-power integral-means results and particular multiply connected Fatou components do not themselves assert that universal comparison.
records.current_title: Universal harmonic-measure spectra and simple connectivity
records.area: Geometric function theory and planar potential theory

records.title: Must an analytic Levi-flat hyperbolic torus bundle be fibered by algebraic curves?
records.review_note: The conjecture concerns the CR foliation of an analytic Levi-flat embedded in an algebraic surface. Abstract foliations on the same torus bundle and existence of one compact leaf do not establish the required algebraic fibration.
records.current_title: Must an analytic Levi-flat hyperbolic torus bundle be fibered by algebraic curves?

records.title: Is maximality local for arbitrary plurisubharmonic functions?
records.review_note: The October local-to-global papers restrict to analytic singularities with bounded remainder or a specified Cegrell class in dimension two. The revised Hilbert-space theorem assumes C2 regularity and additional spectral or boundedness conditions; arbitrary singular psh functions remain outside those hypotheses.
records.current_title: Is maximality local for arbitrary plurisubharmonic functions?

records.title: Exceptional minimal sets on the complex projective plane
records.review_note: The July primary survey retains the unrestricted CP2 question. Results in ambient dimension at least three or with a transverse affine structure do not exclude every exceptional minimal set in the plane.
records.current_title: Exceptional minimal sets on the complex projective plane

records.title: Continuous subsolutions for the complex Monge–Ampère Dirichlet problem
records.review_note: Available continuous-subsolution statements retain Dini or Holder modulus restrictions, smooth-domain conditions, or densities in a restricted class. No matching assertion with only continuous subsolution on every bounded hyperconvex domain was located.
records.current_title: Continuous subsolutions for the complex Monge–Ampère Dirichlet problem

records.title: Can a rational Julia set be an indecomposable continuum?
records.review_note: The rational question is about the entire Julia set, not an indecomposable subcontinuum. Exclusion of the Knaster continuum, polynomial-like criteria and obstructed topological branched coverings do not decide unrestricted rational existence.
records.current_title: Can a rational Julia set be an indecomposable continuum?

records.title: Polynomial Dirichlet solvability characterizes smooth three-dimensional ellipsoids
records.review_note: The August Shao-Zhan announcement is planar. Restricting a three-dimensional harmonic polynomial to a plane need not preserve harmonicity, so it does not settle the smooth three-dimensional Khavinson-Shapiro assertion without a degree bound.
records.current_title: Polynomial Dirichlet solvability characterizes smooth three-dimensional ellipsoids

records.title: Real C¹,¹ regularity of complex Hessian obstacle envelopes
records.review_note: The June complex Hessian flow paper, Lemma 8.1, supplies continuity of the obstacle envelope, not bounds on all real second derivatives. Compact-background complex Hessian estimates and the withdrawn 2017 envelope proof do not give this bounded-domain real C1,1 conclusion.
records.current_title: Real C¹,¹ regularity of complex Hessian obstacle envelopes
records.area: Complex analysis, potential theory and nonlinear obstacle problems

records.title: Vanishing Bergman logarithmic term forces spherical boundary in higher dimensions
records.review_note: The current strong Ramadanov paper treats real ellipsoids in C2. Cheng metric rigidity, general complex-manifold examples and stronger metric hypotheses do not settle flat Bergman logarithmic coefficient implying spherical boundary in every dimension at least three.
records.current_title: Vanishing Bergman logarithmic term forces spherical boundary in higher dimensions

records.title: Does every smooth real-algebraic CR submanifold have Nash–Artin approximation?
records.review_note: The CR condition at the exceptional point is essential. Constant-orbit-dimension and hypersurface approximation theorems, and counterexamples outside the CR class, do not settle every smooth real-algebraic CR submanifold.
records.current_title: Does every smooth real-algebraic CR submanifold have Nash–Artin approximation?

records.title: Is polynomial local mass almost necessary for regular orthogonal polynomials?
records.review_note: The required necessary condition uses polynomial local-mass thresholds and an iterated limit. Fixed-exponent sufficient Bernstein-Markov criteria, exponential-threshold necessity and unbounded spectral regularity do not establish it.
records.current_title: Is polynomial local mass almost necessary for regular orthogonal polynomials?
records.area: Orthogonal polynomials and logarithmic potential theory

records.title: Logarithmic comparison and strong Euler homogeneity of free divisors
records.review_note: The inspected current v5 retains Conjecture 1.2 and proves dimensions up to four, weak Koszul freeness, punctured-neighborhood cases and dimension-five linear free divisors. Counterexamples to all linear divisors satisfying LCT do not refute the conditional implication.
records.current_title: Logarithmic comparison and strong Euler homogeneity of free divisors

records.title: Smooth solutions and fibrewise positivity for homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère
records.review_note: Existing degeneration examples lack the requested global smoothness. Small-boundary-data lower bounds and flat-affine or annulus results do not decide a smooth fibre-degenerate solution on P1 times the closed disc for arbitrary positive boundary data.
records.current_title: Smooth solutions and fibrewise positivity for homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère

records.title: Positive-area images of non-removable Jordan curves
records.review_note: The 2026 flexible-curve result is a special case. The target asks for a positive-area image for every nonremovable Jordan curve; generic nonunique welding is not this stronger conclusion.
records.current_title: Positive-area images of non-removable Jordan curves
records.area: Complex analysis, conformal welding and geometric measure theory

records.title: Do continuous polynomial roots have weak endpoint derivative regularity?
records.review_note: The September reparameterization theorem assumes Cd coefficients and changes the time parameter. It retains subcritical Sobolev bounds and does not imply weak endpoint derivative regularity in the original parameter under C(n-1,1) coefficients.
records.current_title: Do continuous polynomial roots have weak endpoint derivative regularity?

records.title: Uniqueness of free-time controlled transport in Eulerian form
records.review_note: The deterministic Eulerian occupation-and-stopping pair includes controls. Uniqueness of the endpoint plan, stochastic diffusion results and smoother dual-potential cases do not alone establish uniqueness among all admissible Eulerian pairs.
records.current_title: Uniqueness of free-time controlled transport in Eulerian form
records.area: Optimal control and continuous optimal transport

records.title: The sharp generic bound on iterated Fuller singularities
records.review_note: The target is the least dimension-only Cantor-Bendixson order for every PMP extremal in an open dense set of vector-field pairs. The known squared-dimension bound and the sharper order for three-dimensional time minimizers do not identify this all-extremal optimum.
records.current_title: The sharp generic bound on iterated Fuller singularities

records.title: Norm convergence of the two-set Douglas–Rachford iteration
records.review_note: Both October primary announcements give fixed closed convex sets with nonempty intersection and actual classical Douglas-Rachford iterates converging weakly but not strongly. This exactly negates the universal norm-convergence target. Archive without assigning an AIM ID; complete-proof correctness is not independently certified here.
records.current_title: Norm convergence of the two-set Douglas–Rachford iteration

records.title: Residual norm attainment and differentiability of the dual norm
records.review_note: The residuality hypothesis is in the dual norm topology for the given arbitrary Banach norm. Ordinary Bishop-Phelps density, separable cases and operator results with additional Radon-Nikodym or differentiability assumptions do not settle the unrestricted implication.
records.current_title: Residual norm attainment and differentiability of the dual norm
records.area: Banach space geometry and continuous optimization

records.title: Does the silver exponent remain optimal when gradient steps may be negative?
records.review_note: The fresh silver-rate theorem covers predetermined nonnegative schedules only. Signed lower bounds with a larger exponent, fixed finite horizons and one-dimensional equality do not give the silver exponent for arbitrary signed schedules in every dimension.
records.current_title: Does the silver exponent remain optimal when gradient steps may be negative?
records.area: Continuous optimization; complexity of first-order methods

records.title: Global positive classical solutions of sixth-order quantum diffusion
records.review_note: The original quantum sixth-order theorem gives local strictly positive classical solutions and global weak nonnegative solutions. Positivity until every finite time for arbitrary positive H2 data in dimensions two and three is not supplied by fourth-order DLSS contraction or discretization results.
records.current_title: Global positive classical solutions of sixth-order quantum diffusion

records.title: Generalized reaction–diffusion solutions from arbitrary integrable data
records.review_note: Generalized existence from merely L1 data is weaker than classical existence but is still beyond the source integrability thresholds. Entropy-dissipating renormalized systems, logarithmic-entropy data and restricted diffusion exponents impose additional conditions absent here.
records.current_title: Generalized reaction–diffusion solutions from arbitrary integrable data

records.title: Excess energy for collapsing elastic phase boundaries
records.review_note: The target is a strict gap above twice the single-interface cell cost for both collapsing double profiles in a frame-indifferent two-well density. The published energy lower bound and equality under extra reduction hypotheses do not settle existence of such a gap; later point-well single-interface results differ.
records.current_title: Excess energy for collapsing elastic phase boundaries
records.area: Nonlinear elasticity and solid–solid phase transitions

records.title: Global strong aggregation–diffusion without detailed balance
records.review_note: The unresolved part is arbitrary-mass global existence for sign-changing compact BV kernels without detailed balance. Smooth W2-infinity kernels, small-mass bounds, torus bifurcation and conditional uniqueness are narrower or different conclusions.
records.current_title: Global strong aggregation–diffusion without detailed balance

records.title: Bernoulli's lemniscate as the longest-lived zero-winding curve diffusion flow
records.review_note: The lifespan target concerns the pure curve diffusion of arbitrary zero-turning immersed curves with the sharp Bernoulli constant. Shrinkers of nonzero turning number, cubic-curvature elastic terms and stability or immortal convergence do not give this lifetime bound.
records.current_title: Bernoulli's lemniscate as the longest-lived zero-winding curve diffusion flow

records.title: Is the extinction-to-propagation threshold sharp for bistable fractional diffusion?
records.review_note: The question concerns equality of extinction and propagation thresholds for one-dimensional fractional diffusion at every amplitude. Local Laplacian sharp-threshold results and finite but separate fractional bounds do not establish it.
records.current_title: Is the extinction-to-propagation threshold sharp for bistable fractional diffusion?

records.title: A bounded-domain nonlocal-to-local limit for degenerate Cahn–Hilliard diffusion
records.review_note: The exact regional bounded-domain operator, vacuum-allowing linear mobility and strong L2-time H1-space limit are essential. Constant mobility, periodic geometry, different dynamic boundaries and stochastic regular-potential results do not supply this statement.
records.current_title: A bounded-domain nonlocal-to-local limit for degenerate Cahn–Hilliard diffusion

records.title: Global convergence to coexistence in a fitness-driven cross-diffusion system
records.review_note: The fitness-driven model fixes symmetric positive-definite constant interactions with spatially varying resources and entropy-admissible weak solutions. The known subcritical-entropy estimate and different adaptive competition models do not remove that threshold for every positive-mass datum.
records.current_title: Global convergence to coexistence in a fitness-driven cross-diffusion system
records.area: Population dynamics and degenerate parabolic systems

records.title: Global triangular reaction–diffusion systems under transport noise
records.review_note: The current triangular stochastic theorem has state-dependent multiplicative noise, rather than species-dependent spatial transport derivatives. records.title: Are compact convex sets in arbitrary linear metric spaces absolute retracts?
records.review_note: The current full-scope Yuan claim was inspected through its supporting Lemmas A.1-A.2 and Theorems A.6-A.7. Lemma A.1 is false even for a connected interval with a two-member proper open cover: any subordinate partition has a tie by the intermediate value theorem. Refinement cannot repair this, because a unique maximal index would be locally constant and hence constant on a connected interval. Therefore this argument does not establish the claimed general AR theorem. Existing locally convex and basis cases remain partial progress.

records.status_addendum: A 2026 general AR claim was also checked in the author-uploaded text [additional reference]. Its Theorem A.7 uses Lemma A.1, which asserts a subordinate continuous partition of unity with a unique largest component everywhere for every finite open cover. This lemma is false. Take K=[0,1] with the relative-open cover U1=[0,2/3), U2=(1/3,1]. For any subordinate partition (phi1,phi2), phi1(0)=1 and phi1(1)=0, so some point has phi1=phi2=1/2. Refining the cover cannot avoid the obstruction: a unique largest index is locally constant, hence constant on connected K, forcing one proper cover member to contain K. Thus the proposed proof does not resolve the general question. This is a specific obstruction to that argument, not a counterexample to the AR conjecture.

This does not resolve the intended rigidity question modulo null boundary changes, or the compact-convex-body version.
records.current_title: Does convexity under every sectionwise contraction characterize ellipsoids?

records.title: Minimum-volume convex bodies of prescribed minimum width
records.review_note: The high-dimensional minimum-volume problem is for minimum width, not constant width. Recent hyperbolic or ball-convex results do not determine the Euclidean sharp constant and all equality cases in every dimension at least three.
records.current_title: Minimum-volume convex bodies of prescribed minimum width

records.title: Smooth classification of four-manifolds with conformal curvature ratio below eight
records.review_note: The known beta less than four sphere theorem and gap results requiring nonzero positive second Betti number or extra curvature assumptions do not supply the complete smooth classification for beta less than eight under the stated conformal assumptions alone.
records.current_title: Smooth classification of four-manifolds with conformal curvature ratio below eight

records.title: Constant nonzero Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature
records.review_note: The new Bismut Hermitian-Einstein examples impose a Ricci condition, not constant Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature. The 2026 BTP results mainly concern Chern curvature with parallel torsion; the locally conformally Kahler Bismut result is a restricted class. None covers arbitrary compact Hermitian manifolds with nonzero constant Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature.
records.current_title: Constant nonzero Bismut holomorphic sectional curvature

records.title: Do nearest-point strata of finitely many convex sites have finitely many components?
records.review_note: The source proves finiteness for X1 and connectedness of X1 union X2, not finiteness of every exact multiplicity stratum. Semialgebraic-site finiteness and non-Euclidean bisector examples impose or change hypotheses. Author/title and current-resolution searches found no matching unrestricted Euclidean theorem or counterexample.
records.current_title: Do nearest-point strata of finitely many convex sites have finitely many components?

records.title: Rational coefficients in supernatural decompositions of sheaf cohomology
records.review_note: Finite rational decompositions of graded local cohomology tables in bounded dimension and pure Betti-table results are different cones. Rational approximation of a real cohomology-table decomposition does not establish rationality of each unique chain coefficient for a general non-pure coherent sheaf.
records.current_title: Rational coefficients in supernatural decompositions of sheaf cohomology
records.area: Algebraic geometry / cohomology of coherent sheaves

records.title: Hyperbolicity of general vortex thermostats
records.review_note: The published 2026 quasi-Fuchsian paper treats holomorphic integral-degree differentials with zero theta, rather than all root-bundle vortex thermostats with arbitrary theta. The general source still gives dominated splitting and conditional Anosovness. Non-Anosov torus thermostats fail the negative-Euler and vortex hypotheses.
records.current_title: Hyperbolicity of general vortex thermostats

records.title: One homothety factor for optimal convex-body covers in every dimension
records.review_note: Naszodi proves a scale for each fixed dimension. Fractional illumination and asymptotic covering estimates permit more than the exact optimal worst-case number and use dimension-dependent shrinkage. They do not supply a single scale at the exact H_d count for all dimensions.
records.current_title: One homothety factor for optimal convex-body covers in every dimension

records.title: Do arbitrary Steiner symmetrization processes converge in shape?
records.review_note: Square-summable angular increments, finitely many directions and finite unions of line segments are conditional positive results. They do not prove shape convergence for every direction sequence simultaneously for all compact initial sets with the source uniform-isometry convention.
records.current_title: Do arbitrary Steiner symmetrization processes converge in shape?

records.title: Positive 2-sections of Lefschetz fibrations over the sphere
records.review_note: The revised 29 October 2026 preprint v2 was read at its renumbered Question 21, page 33. It explicitly retains the 2-section question and its equivalence to fiber divisibility dividing two. New sectionless examples still admit 2-sections; the stronger primitivity assertion still has a documented gap.

records.title: Log-squared systolic growth on translation surfaces
records.review_note: The known large-systole translation-surface construction has order log(g)/(g log log(g)) on a subsequence of genera. Saddle-connection and hyperbolic-surface results do not yield the requested log-squared closed-loop systolic ratio in every sufficiently large genus.
records.current_title: Log-squared systolic growth on translation surfaces

records.title: Can every bi-Perron unit occur as a surface stretch factor after taking a power?
records.review_note: Current compact-surface results cover bi-Perron numbers with real or unimodular conjugates. The 2026 weak-Perron realization uses infinite-type end-periodic surfaces, outside this compact-surface target. The withdrawn degree-three claim is not an active resolution.
records.current_title: Can every bi-Perron unit occur as a surface stretch factor after taking a power?

records.title: Must two commuting vector fields on a three-manifold have a common zero when one has nonzero index?
records.review_note: The common-zero theorems impose a collinearity surface or C3 regularity plus a partially hyperbolic periodic-orbit or transverse-plane-field condition. They do not establish the arbitrary commuting C1 pair assertion. No matching full result was located.
records.current_title: Must two commuting vector fields on a three-manifold have a common zero when one has nonzero index?

records.title: Does every tight contact 3-manifold have finite Giroux torsion?
records.review_note: Finiteness of the number of tight structures at a prescribed finite torsion value and torsion-free veering-triangulation results do not bound the torsion of each arbitrary tight contact structure. The 2026 K3 list explicitly retains the exact question.
records.current_title: Does every tight contact 3-manifold have finite Giroux torsion?

records.title: Classifying rotation-equivariant Minkowski valuations
records.review_note: The 2026 Lefschetz-operators paper explicitly retains the complete rotation-equivariant Minkowski-valuation classification. Convolution representations leave admissibility of generating functions unresolved. Affinely contravariant function-valued and lattice-polytope classifications have stronger symmetry or different domains.
records.current_title: Classifying rotation-equivariant Minkowski valuations

records.title: Do bounded minimal graphs over the hyperbolic disk have radial limits almost everywhere?
records.review_note: The known Fatou theorem on a Euclidean disk and the hyperbolic unbounded counterexample do not answer the bounded complete-hyperbolic-disk target. Metric-density hypotheses in the later PDE theorem fail for the complete Poincare disk; special polygon vertices do not cover arbitrary graphs.
records.current_title: Do bounded minimal graphs over the hyperbolic disk have radial limits almost everywhere?
records.area: Geometric analysis and boundary behavior of nonlinear elliptic equations

records.title: Can bounded complementary components of balls be controlled uniformly under nonnegative Ricci curvature?
records.review_note: Minerbe requires reverse volume growth with an exponent greater than one and obtains a constant depending on that data. One-endedness alone does not control depths of bounded complementary components by a dimension-only factor. No matching unrestricted result was located.
records.current_title: Can bounded complementary components of balls be controlled uniformly under nonnegative Ricci curvature?

records.title: Magnetic flatness from everywhere-collapsed Green directions
records.review_note: The 2026 thermostat source still separates the magnetic everywhere-Green-collapse implication from its nonpositive-curvature theorem. The entropy identity uses a no-focal-points condition and the horocycle rigidity theorem imposes an action condition. Neither gives the implication under no conjugate points alone.
records.current_title: Magnetic flatness from everywhere-collapsed Green directions

records.title: Does Morse index control topology in every fixed positive-Ricci manifold?
records.review_note: The 2026 index-one counterexamples vary the ambient manifold and metric. They refute a dimension-only estimate, but do not refute this fixed-ambient conjecture. Symmetric-space and ACS special cases and estimates with an area-dependent constant leave the target.
records.current_title: Does Morse index control topology in every fixed positive-Ricci manifold?

records.title: Sheaf-theoretic SL(2,C) Floer cohomology detects the three-sphere
records.review_note: Nonempty irreducible SL2 character schemes do not imply nonzero hypercohomology of the vanishing-cycle sheaf. Special surgery calculations and proposed comparisons with a different instanton theory do not prove general detection by the unframed Abouzaid-Manolescu invariant.
records.current_title: Sheaf-theoretic SL(2,C) Floer cohomology detects the three-sphere

records.title: Does the marked area spectrum determine a symplectic billiard table up to affine equivalence?
records.review_note: The 2026 spectral-rigidity theorem concerns isospectral families in an axially symmetric near-ellipse class. It does not prove global injectivity of the sequence of maximal polygon areas for arbitrary pairs of strictly convex tables. Hyperbolic marked-area-spectrum rigidity is a different invariant.
records.current_title: Does the marked area spectrum determine a symplectic billiard table up to affine equivalence?
records.area: Symplectic billiards and geometric inverse problems

records.title: A compact subset that cannot escape to infinity by homotopy
records.review_note: Periodic maximal flats establish a nonperipheral compact subset in the locally symmetric case. Counterexamples to loop-only nonperipherality and examples without a uniform lower sectional bound do not refute this tame bounded-curvature compact-subset assertion.
records.current_title: A compact subset that cannot escape to infinity by homotopy
records.area: Riemannian geometry and topology of noncompact manifolds

records.title: Controlled global Coulomb gauges in ordinary Lorentz weak L4
records.review_note: The original global gauge theorem lacks the Coulomb condition; Wang controls a different integrability-radius space rather than the ordinary Lorentz norm. Small-curvature gauge estimates do not cover every finite curvature-energy bound. The conjunction requested remains unmatched.
records.current_title: Controlled global Coulomb gauges in ordinary Lorentz weak L4

records.title: Is the maximally stable catenoid least-area among all minimal surfaces spanning a slab?
records.review_note: The known slab-area extensions require the same orientation for all horizontal section components or restrict to annuli. Mixed-orientation and general-topology competitors remain outside those theorems; the general Bernstein-Breiner conjecture was not matched by a complete result.
records.current_title: Is the maximally stable catenoid least-area among all minimal surfaces spanning a slab?

records.title: The \(4\pi\) boundary-curvature threshold for oriented minimal surfaces
records.review_note: White improves the disk threshold beyond three pi, but not to four pi. Embeddedness at total boundary curvature at most four pi is not a disk-topology theorem. Nonorientable Mobius-strip examples do not refute the oriented target.
records.current_title: The $`4\pi`$ boundary-curvature threshold for oriented minimal surfaces

records.title: Quaternionic Calabi equation on compact HKT manifolds
records.review_note: The September 2026 theorem gives continuous solutions with local flatness, and the October 2026 smooth result requires a compatible locally conformally hyperKahler metric. The hyperKahler case is also known; none supplies smooth existence on every HKT manifold in the displayed holomorphic-volume class.
records.current_title: Quaternionic Calabi equation on compact HKT manifolds

records.title: Are all flat SU(2) Chern–Simons values on closed three-manifolds rational?
records.review_note: Graph-manifold and Seifert rationality do not cover every three-manifold. A high-precision numerical candidate cannot establish irrationality of an exact SU2 critical value. Complex SL2 Chern-Simons values are not counterexamples for the compact SU2 target.
records.current_title: Are all flat SU(2) Chern–Simons values on closed three-manifolds rational?

records.title: Straight-triangle realizations of triangulated double tori
records.review_note: All ten-vertex genus-two triangulations are realizable, but this finite subfamily does not imply every triangulation is. Surface-graph framework rigidity and intrinsic holonomy-signature realizability do not embed the specified flat triangular complex without subdivision.
records.current_title: Straight-triangle realizations of triangulated double tori

records.title: Exponential-time hyperbolic pseudolocality in higher dimensions
records.review_note: The higher-dimensional hyperbolic-pseudolocality statement remains distinct from the established surface theorem. General local-existence estimates and global-small-perturbation hyperbolic stability do not yield an exponential time bound for every given complete flow from a ball hypothesis alone.
records.current_title: Exponential-time hyperbolic pseudolocality in higher dimensions

records.title: Continuous densities for inhomogeneous grid projections
records.review_note: Lq projected densities outside a zero-dimensional exceptional set need not be continuous. Homogeneous-retention results and random-shadow interval results differ from the arbitrary deterministic grid weights. The 2015 inhomogeneous claim was withdrawn and is not used as a resolution.
records.current_title: Continuous densities for inhomogeneous grid projections

records.title: Must a four-dimensional steady soliton with positive Ricci curvature and linear curvature decay be Bryant?
records.review_note: Law v3 remains the latest revision and explicitly states that dropping its weighted Lichnerowicz-kernel dimension hypothesis is unknown. Positivity of sectional curvature only outside a compact set does not supply the global sign assumptions in other Bryant-rigidity results.
records.current_title: Must a four-dimensional steady soliton with positive Ricci curvature and linear curvature decay be Bryant?

records.title: Unknotting number and genus of positive fibered knots
records.review_note: The latest accepted Kegel et al. text was reread: Theorem 1.5 is a fixed-diagram obstruction, and Conjecture 1.6 separately proposes that the unrestricted unknotting number is nine. A secondary disproof label is not supported by the primary theorem; general u=g remains unmatched.
records.current_title: Unknotting number and genus of positive fibered knots

records.title: Do monotone tori minimize Hamiltonian volume in complex hyperbolic space?
records.review_note: The source shows equal-radius Hamiltonian stability, not a global Hamiltonian volume minimum. Volume-decreasing unequal-radius tori and Euclidean results do not settle the monotone complex-hyperbolic target; the symplectic comparison map is not an isometry.
records.current_title: Do monotone tori minimize Hamiltonian volume in complex hyperbolic space?

records.title: Does absence of a rational first integral force a foliation's tangent sheaf to split?
records.review_note: The splitting result for a nonzero tangent vector field or degree at most three does not cover arbitrary-degree foliations. Known non-split distributions need integrability and the absence of invariant hypersurfaces or rational first integrals before they could refute either stated clause.
records.current_title: Does absence of a rational first integral force a foliation's tangent sheaf to split?

records.title: Maximal extensions of fine moduli spaces of coherent sheaves
records.review_note: Special maximal fine-moduli constructions do not imply that every open fine-moduli class has a maximal extension. Taking an increasing union need not preserve finite type or a global universal sheaf. No matching general extension theorem or counterexample was located.
records.current_title: Maximal extensions of fine moduli spaces of coherent sheaves

records.title: Does the ∂∂̄-lemma imply the existence of a balanced metric?
records.review_note: The source asks existence of some balanced metric, not equality of positive cones. Deformation or bimeromorphic-invariance counterexamples to the ddbar lemma and failures of a stronger cone identity do not imply a nonbalanced ddbar manifold. Restricted solvmanifold and hypercomplex theorems do not settle the full implication.
records.current_title: Does the ∂∂̄-lemma imply the existence of a balanced metric?

records.title: Relative connectedness of annuli in Ricci-nonnegative ends
records.review_note: The source proves endwise relatively connected annuli with finite first Betti number or stronger asymptotically nonnegative sectional curvature. Later heat-kernel and Riesz-transform applications retain RCA as an extra premise; these are not proofs of the unrestricted Ricci-outside-compact implication.
records.current_title: Relative connectedness of annuli in Ricci-nonnegative ends
records.area: Geometric analysis and heat kernels on manifolds

records.title: Must every Reeb flow on a closed non-lens-space 3-manifold have infinitely many simple periodic orbits?
records.review_note: Exactly-two-orbit classification does not rule out finite counts larger than two. The available two-or-infinity theorems require torsion first Chern class or a nondegeneracy hypothesis; the August 2026 result still has strong nondegeneracy. The problem removes both restrictions simultaneously.
records.current_title: Must every Reeb flow on a closed non-lens-space 3-manifold have infinitely many simple periodic orbits?

records.title: Must every analytic compactification of complex affine space be Moishezon?
records.review_note: Smooth Kahler-boundary compactification and equivariant cases are restricted. Non-Moishezon compactifications of (C-star)^4 have a different open part, while nonprojective Moishezon compactifications still satisfy the requested conclusion. No full affine-space result was located.
records.current_title: Must every analytic compactification of complex affine space be Moishezon?

records.title: Can a small $C^1$ perturbation make any prescribed orbit asymptotic to a hyperbolic periodic orbit?
records.review_note: The ergodic/asymptotic closing statements give frequency-one closability or exponent approximation for almost every point, rather than stable capture of every prescribed point after an arbitrarily small C1 perturbation. Generic and dissipative-surface results do not cover the universal statement.
records.current_title: Can a small $`C^1`$ perturbation make any prescribed orbit asymptotic to a hyperbolic periodic orbit?

records.title: Can three positive minimal graphs have disjoint planar supports?
records.review_note: The two October 2026 papers remain partial: one treats growth properties for simply connected supports, the other specified slope regimes. These conditions do not exhaust arbitrary hypothetical triples. Vanishing-curvature-at-infinity results impose another omitted hypothesis.
records.current_title: Can three positive minimal graphs have disjoint planar supports?

records.title: The bounded-isometry conjecture for closed symplectic manifolds
records.review_note: The full bounded-isometry conjecture is distinct from versions for the spectral metric. The Kodaira-Thurston, linear four-torus and condition-(H) theorems cover specified manifolds, not all closed symplectic manifolds.
records.current_title: The bounded-isometry conjecture for closed symplectic manifolds

records.title: Amenable normal subgroups and zero simplicial volume
records.review_note: The complete-affine vanishing theorem imposes an affine structure. General measurable-action and quotient-cohomology criteria are sufficient conditions, without constructing them for every infinite amenable normal subgroup. No unrestricted aspherical-manifold resolution was located.
records.current_title: Amenable normal subgroups and zero simplicial volume

records.title: Does Pu’s sharp systolic bound hold for every nonfree two-complex?
records.review_note: Known universal systolic-area lower bounds and cup-length special cases do not reach the sharp 2/pi bound for every nonfree two-complex. The real projective plane establishes sharpness if the inequality holds, not the universal upper estimate on systolic ratio.
records.current_title: Does Pu’s sharp systolic bound hold for every nonfree two-complex?

records.title: Can every interior Neumann–Steklov eigenvalue pair be realized by a planar domain?
records.review_note: The known closure of the joint attainable diagram does not imply every interior point is attained exactly. Collapsing convex-domain ratio estimates and one-dimensional profile bounds have different hypotheses and conclusions.
records.current_title: Can every interior Neumann–Steklov eigenvalue pair be realized by a planar domain?

records.title: Uniqueness of the critical Möbius band at Morse index five
records.review_note: The index-five computation does not identify every index-five surface. First-Steklov-coordinate, rotational-symmetry and local-uniqueness results add hypotheses. The genus-zero critical-catenoid announcement concerns B3, not nonorientable codimension-two surfaces in B4.
records.current_title: Uniqueness of the critical Möbius band at Morse index five

records.title: Infinitesimal rigidity of weakly convex decomposable polyhedra
records.review_note: The available rigidity theorem adds weak codecomposability, and recent experimental work does not prove the full weakly convex decomposable conjecture. Edge-and-coplanarity rigidity results constrain more than the boundary-edge velocity equations in this target.
records.current_title: Infinitesimal rigidity of weakly convex decomposable polyhedra

records.title: Free Lie subalgebras in rational homotopy
records.review_note: The classical simply connected finite-complex Avramov-Felix conjecture is still explicitly retained in the 2023 survey. Additional topological-complexity assumptions give cases, but not an arbitrary rationally hyperbolic finite complex. Broader enriched-Lie conventions do not settle this subalgebra assertion.
records.current_title: Free Lie subalgebras in rational homotopy

records.title: Does positive magnetic curvature force contact type on a magnetic energy level of the sphere?
records.review_note: Benedetti proves low-energy and special-geometry contact type. A noncontact example without positive magnetic curvature is not a counterexample to the implication here. Results for exact fields or merely existence of a periodic orbit have different assumptions or conclusions.
records.current_title: Does positive magnetic curvature force contact type on a magnetic energy level of the sphere?

records.title: The Debarre–de Jong dimension conjecture for lines on smooth Fano hypersurfaces
records.review_note: Chenglong Yu, arXiv:2610.38812v1, submitted 28 October 2026, Theorem 1.3(i), announces nonemptiness and pure expected dimension 2n-d-3 for every smooth complex degree-d hypersurface with 2<=d<=n. Degree one is elementary. Any counterexample over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field descends to finitely many characteristic-zero coefficients, embeds into C and preserves Krull dimension after algebraically closed base change; thus the complex theorem covers the admitted field scope. Archive without ID as a matching complete announcement, without certifying its full proof.
records.current_title: The Debarre–de Jong dimension conjecture for lines on smooth Fano hypersurfaces

records.title: Bounded additive graph approximation of Euclidean three-space
records.review_note: The two-dimensional graph approximation and the Gromov-hyperbolic theorem do not cover Euclidean three-space. Periodic-graph obstructions do not exclude arbitrary nonperiodic graphs; the Squishy Grid theorem uses a planar nearest-neighbor graph and distance-dependent error.
records.current_title: Bounded additive graph approximation of Euclidean three-space

records.title: A three-condition criterion for extremal toric Poincaré metrics
records.review_note: Hirzebruch-surface constructions establish cases, while Donaldson metrics can have different asymptotics. The Poincare extremal uniqueness theorem and J-equation solvability do not prove existence from all three stated stability and boundary-affine conditions.
records.current_title: A three-condition criterion for extremal toric Poincaré metrics

records.title: Stein fillability of all sufficiently large surgeries on a knot
records.review_note: Positive contact-surgery fillability criteria impose conditions on a Legendrian representative or a Lagrangian disk. They do not show that every sufficiently large rational surgery on every smooth knot admits some Stein-fillable structure. Known selected knot families leave the universal threshold question.
records.current_title: Stein fillability of all sufficiently large surgeries on a knot

records.title: Does regular quantization force a compact Kähler metric to be homogeneous?
records.review_note: The September 2026 toric positive-first-Chern-ray theorem explicitly retains unrestricted regular quantization. Noncompact Simanca examples do not refute compact homogeneity, and varying balanced approximations do not imply the fixed-metric regular-quantization premise.
records.current_title: Does regular quantization force a compact Kähler metric to be homogeneous?

records.title: Does the Weeks manifold uniquely realize the three-dimensional Margulis constant?
records.review_note: The September 2026 verified census calculation gives an upper bound for the universal Margulis constant and a minimum among selected censuses. Its global equality remains Conjecture 1.4; neither that calculation nor the symmetric-pair theorem proves global uniqueness of the Weeks realization.
records.current_title: Does the Weeks manifold uniquely realize the three-dimensional Margulis constant?

records.title: Does vanishing real simplicial volume force vanishing integral foliated simplicial volume?
records.review_note: Amenable-cover and mapping-torus results give restricted vanishing families. Scalar-curvature criteria in the OpenAI collection impose additional geometry and do not infer integral foliated vanishing solely from zero real simplicial volume. Stable integral volume over finite covers is a different invariant.
records.current_title: Does vanishing real simplicial volume force vanishing integral foliated simplicial volume?

records.title: Is the group of interval exchange transformations amenable?
records.review_note: The January 2026 subgroup theorem covers selected elementary-amenable families. The source rational-rank-at-most-two result is also restricted, and the Prove2Me mission remains a question/formalization route rather than a matching proved full-group amenability theorem.
records.current_title: Is the group of interval exchange transformations amenable?

records.title: The doubling conjecture for positive scalar curvature
records.review_note: Frenck April 2026 Theorems A-C assume conditions on boundary fundamental-group images, dimension, spin or cohomology, or treat selected four-manifolds. They do not establish the arbitrary-manifold doubling implication. The source retains Conjecture 7.1.
records.current_title: The doubling conjecture for positive scalar curvature

records.title: Are saddle-connection lengths uniformly distributed modulo one on every flat surface?
records.review_note: The all-SL2-orbits theorem is almost everywhere within each orbit, not every individual flat surface. Its newer indexed record repeats that almost-everywhere quantifier. No matching every-surface proof or counterexample was located.
records.current_title: Are saddle-connection lengths uniformly distributed modulo one on every flat surface?

records.title: Bondal–Orlov localization for rational singularities
records.review_note: Shen-Sun prove localization with cohomological dimension at most two for the whole pushforward functor. Rational singularities only impose vanishing on the structure sheaf. The threefold theorem and K-theoretic or thick-generation statements do not settle the unrestricted bounded Verdier-quotient equivalence.
records.current_title: Bondal–Orlov localization for rational singularities

records.title: Are nontrivial planar lattice self-similar sets non-Minkowski-measurable?
records.review_note: The October 2026 regular n-flake article remains a special planar family, and the pluriphase theorem retains a geometric hypothesis. The one-dimensional full converse does not cover all planar open-set-condition lattice systems with dimension strictly between one and two.
records.current_title: Are nontrivial planar lattice self-similar sets non-Minkowski-measurable?

records.title: Is the algebraic Hilbert number exactly the Harnack-type expression?
records.review_note: The generic or nodal invariant-curve theorems do not establish the unrestricted algebraic Hilbert number. The Prove2Me listing presents the exact formula as a goal, not an independently checked solution. The older Winkel counterexample concerns a different conjecture.
records.current_title: Is the algebraic Hilbert number exactly the Harnack-type expression?

records.title: Scalar-flat realization of extendible Bartnik boundary data
records.review_note: Existing scalar-flat extensions require positive intrinsic Gauss curvature or local perturbation of a static background. Separate prescriptions of the boundary metric or mean curvature do not preserve both simultaneously. Capacity-maximization results solve a different extremal problem.
records.current_title: Scalar-flat realization of extendible Bartnik boundary data

records.title: A parallel null direction in higher-order symmetric spacetimes
records.review_note: Third-order symmetry and second-order torsion-connection results do not prove a parallel null direction for every proper Levi-Civita order at least four. The higher-order discussion in the current primary survey remains conjectural.
records.current_title: A parallel null direction in higher-order symmetric spacetimes

records.title: Path connectedness of the full asymptotically flat vacuum constraint space
records.review_note: Maximal-data path connectedness and contractibility retain trace-free extrinsic curvature. The recent high-dimensional closed-manifold topology theorem concerns another manifold and topology. No path from arbitrary nonmaximal one-ended data into the maximal subspace is supplied.
records.current_title: Path connectedness of the full asymptotically flat vacuum constraint space

records.title: Volume-preserving intrinsic-flat compactness with minimal boundary
records.review_note: Wenger compactness gives a convergent subsequence but only lower semicontinuity of mass. Later scalar-preservation or boundary-VADB results assume volume convergence; they cannot establish the missing equality here. Drawstring counterexamples in other geometries do not satisfy the full minimal-boundary and no-interior-minimal-surface hypotheses.
records.current_title: Volume-preserving intrinsic-flat compactness with minimal boundary

records.title: Future timelike completeness and a CMC Cauchy hypersurface
records.review_note: The CMC theorem for an initially nonnegatively expanding Cauchy slice adds a sign hypothesis absent from the future-complete conjecture. The timelike-sectional-curvature and conditional Busemann results are also restricted. The announced June Bartnik proof is still withdrawn, and would in any case need comparison with the stronger future-only CMC target.
records.current_title: Future timelike completeness and a CMC Cauchy hypersurface

records.title: Zero vacuum Bartnik mass without a no-horizon condition
records.review_note: Attained zero ADM mass is covered by positive-mass rigidity, but the problem includes nonattained infima over scalar-flat exteriors allowing horizons. Dong-Song restrict admissible exteriors by excluding minimal surfaces. The newly published spacetime black-hole paper treats compact apparent-horizon boundary or noncompact domains with horizons in each admissible extension, not strictly mean-convex compact three-balls with this exact vacuum exterior infimum.
records.current_title: Zero vacuum Bartnik mass without a no-horizon condition

records.title: Real-energy nullspace on nontrapping Lorentzian scattering spaces
records.review_note: Essential self-adjointness and nonreal resolvent invertibility do not exclude a rapidly decaying real-energy nullspace. Taira leaves possible embedded eigenvalues without extra assumptions. Radiative asymptotically flat invertibility theorems impose more structured asymptotics and causality than the general source/sink scattering model.
records.current_title: Real-energy nullspace on nontrapping Lorentzian scattering spaces

records.title: Scalar-flat apparent-horizon extensions with prescribed Schwarzschild mass
records.review_note: The nonnegative-scalar-curvature construction permits positive scalar curvature in a collar. Miao-Xie achieve scalar-flat minimal-boundary extensions for positive Gauss curvature but not the entire spectral class with prescribed Schwarzschild mass and global mean-convex foliation. Exterior gluing alone leaves interior scalar curvature unchanged.
records.current_title: Scalar-flat apparent-horizon extensions with prescribed Schwarzschild mass

records.title: Uniqueness of the simply connected static three-dimensional hemisphere
records.review_note: The known hemisphere results require a curvature, surface-gravity or boundary-gradient bound. Recent boundary-static Robin or quasi-Einstein results change the equation or exclude the static parameter. Nariai quotients fail simple connectedness; higher-dimensional counterexamples do not address dimension three.
records.current_title: Uniqueness of the simply connected static three-dimensional hemisphere

records.title: Intrinsic-flat stability of scalar sphere rigidity
records.review_note: Rotationally symmetric width stability is established. Width-only counterexamples have minimum minimal-surface area tending to zero; Llarull stability imposes a degree/map comparison assumption. Neither class settles the stated unrestricted three-sphere minimum-area conjecture.
records.current_title: Intrinsic-flat stability of scalar sphere rigidity

records.title: Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture
records.review_note: The June McCann-Ohanyan announcement remains explicitly withdrawn in the current primary record because its starting proposition is false. The follow-up paper formulates equivalent open assertions. Conditional line, symmetry, Busemann and sectional-curvature splitting results do not establish the three assumptions alone.
records.current_title: Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture

records.title: Completeness under conformal changes of compact Lorentzian spaceforms
records.review_note: Null completeness is conformally preserved here, while full affine geodesic completeness is stronger. Timelike conformal Killing fields or global homogeneous metrics are additional assumptions not implied by local constant curvature on a compact quotient. Null-distance completeness is another conclusion.
records.current_title: Completeness under conformal changes of compact Lorentzian spaceforms

records.title: Must observations be affine in every finite-dimensional Euclidean estimation algebra?
records.review_note: Ocone gives quadratic multiplication functions, not affine observations. Maximal-rank and dimension-four rank-three results add rank assumptions; compact-manifold nonexistence does not cover arbitrary Euclidean observations. No full weak-Mitter result under these general hypotheses was located.

records.title: Even trace coefficients for arbitrary Hermitian matrix pairs
records.review_note: Dinh, Le and Vuong, Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture, 22 October 2026, Theorem 4.3 claims for every Hermitian pair the pinching inequality whenever the second-variable second derivative of a scalar polynomial is globally nonnegative. Take p(s,t)=s^(m-k)t^k with both exponents even. Then its second derivative is nonnegative, and the commuting pinched trace Tr(A^(m-k) E_A(B)^k) is nonnegative. The symmetrized word coefficient is thus nonnegative in every dimension, including k=0 trivially. This exactly implies the submitted even-BMV assertion for indefinite Hermitian matrices. Archive as a matching complete announcement, not an independently certified proof, and allocate no AIM ID.
records.archive_clarification: The paper phrases its named corrected-BMV theorem for positive matrices, but its stated all-Hermitian Theorem 4.3 also implies this different even-coefficient target by the monomial substitution recorded in the review.
